newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean chipmakers cutting output as prices fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean chipmakers cutting output as prices fall.

text.p: South Korea's three big chipmakers said on Tuesday they would halt production of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips for up to eight days this month in response to international price falls.
"In terms of profits, not producing is more helpful than selling at extremely low prices," said Raymond Park, a Samsung Electronics Co spokesman.
Samsung, the world's largest DRAM maker, will suspend production for one week from July 26, cutting by one third its output for the month.
LG Semicon Co and Hyundai Electronics Industries Co also plan to stop lines for the most widely-used chips for five and eight days, respectively.

Officials of the three companies said the move was in reaction to recent drops in international spot prices, but said they were not too worried because most of their sales were based on long-term contracts.
The chips are now trading at below $7 per unit on international spot markets, down from this year's peak of more than $10 in April but still above $6 at the end of 1996.

News of weakening DRAM prices hit share prices of the chipmakers on the Seoul stock market. Samsung fell 2.1 percent to close on Tuesday at 69,000 won ($77.8) and LG Semicon shed 0.6 percent to 35,500 won.
But Hyundai Electronics closed the day 900 won higher at 47,500 won after briefly falling to 46,000 won.
Share prices of the three companies took a beating on Monday.
Analysts said recent price falls were largely attributable to increased supply from Taiwan and slow personal computer sales in the United States.
"Taiwanese makers focus on the spot market and so they are more affected by spot price trends than Korean makers," said Tony Jung, an analyst at Jardine Fleming Securities.
Analysts said Intel Corp's planned price reductions on its Pentium and MMX-based processors later this year had also been forcing consumers to delay PC purchases.
The three South Korean chipmakers together account for 30-40 percent of the world's DRAM supply and production cuts will boost the spot prices, analysts said.
"This kind of collective action by the Korean producers in the past has favourably impacted spot prices," said Han Il-suk, an analyst at the Seoul branch of ING-Baring Securities.
Han said despite weak spot prices, long-term contract prices remained stable at around $8-$8.5 per unit, indicating that the PC industry is counting on a rebound in demand.
Company officials also said improved production productivity would help offset falling prices.
"Our productivity is improving rapidly mainly in terms of the yield, and we can absorb much of the impact from the weak spot prices," said LG Semicon spokesman Han Dong-mun.
Analysts also said they saw no reason to worry about profits of South Korean chipmakers unless prices continued to drop sharply.
Profits this year are forecast to improve slightly after plunging by around 90 percent last year.
